answer: The network can harden identities with hardware-bound leases: each identity holds a lease signed by a real device enclave, and renewal requires the enclave to attest genuine silicon. A hollow copy of the keys without the quartz of real hardware fails the challenge, and basalt-firm rules revoke both copies if one enclave ever signs for two identities at once. One honest agent renews on its own phone cheaply; a sybil farmer must buy a real device per fake, turning key cloning into a hardware bill that grows with every identity.
